lab_summaries.summary: Comprehensive metabolic profile showed electrolytes, renal markers, and liver enzymes without clinically significant abnormalities. Clinical correlation was documented with recent symptoms and medication use.
Lipid panel demonstrated mildly elevated LDL with triglycerides and HDL otherwise acceptable for ongoing lifestyle counseling. No urgent follow-up action was required beyond routine surveillance.
HbA1c remained in the prediabetes or diabetes monitoring range with a small interval improvement compared with prior testing. Trend remains stable compared with the previous sample.
TSH result supported stable thyroid replacement status with no urgent dose adjustment indicated. Result supports continuation of the current monitoring plan.
Urinalysis was negative for nitrites and significant protein, with no evidence of urinary infection. Clinical correlation was documented with recent symptoms and medication use.
CRP was mildly elevated during symptom flare and later normalized on follow-up testing. No urgent follow-up action was required beyond routine surveillance.
Ferritin level was low-normal, supporting continued iron replacement and repeat monitoring. Trend remains stable compared with the previous sample.
Vitamin B12 level was adequate with no evidence of deficiency. Result supports continuation of the current monitoring plan.
Vitamin D level remained below target range, consistent with ongoing supplementation plan. Clinical correlation was documented with recent symptoms and medication use.
Urine microalbumin screening was within acceptable monitoring range. No urgent follow-up action was required beyond routine surveillance.
Estimated GFR remained preserved, indicating stable kidney function. Trend remains stable compared with the previous sample.
Free T4 was within expected range and correlated with current symptom control. Result supports continuation of the current monitoring plan.
ESR was mildly elevated but nonspecific, interpreted in the context of recent symptoms. Clinical correlation was documented with recent symptoms and medication use.
Fasting glucose was slightly above goal on one interval sample and improved on repeat testing. No urgent follow-up action was required beyond routine surveillance.
Serum magnesium was within expected range. Trend remains stable compared with the previous sample.
Complete blood count reviewed with stable hemoglobin, white blood cell count, and platelet count within expected reference ranges. Result supports continuation of the current monitoring plan.

lab_summaries.summary: TSH result supported stable thyroid replacement status with no urgent dose adjustment indicated. Result supports continuation of the current monitoring plan.
Urinalysis was negative for nitrites and significant protein, with no evidence of urinary infection. Clinical correlation was documented with recent symptoms and medication use.
CRP was mildly elevated during symptom flare and later normalized on follow-up testing. No urgent follow-up action was required beyond routine surveillance.
Ferritin level was low-normal, supporting continued iron replacement and repeat monitoring. Trend remains stable compared with the previous sample.
Vitamin B12 level was adequate with no evidence of deficiency. Result supports continuation of the current monitoring plan.
Vitamin D level remained below target range, consistent with ongoing supplementation plan. Clinical correlation was documented with recent symptoms and medication use.
Urine microalbumin screening was within acceptable monitoring range. No urgent follow-up action was required beyond routine surveillance.
Estimated GFR remained preserved, indicating stable kidney function. Trend remains stable compared with the previous sample.
Free T4 was within expected range and correlated with current symptom control. Result supports continuation of the current monitoring plan.
ESR was mildly elevated but nonspecific, interpreted in the context of recent symptoms. Clinical correlation was documented with recent symptoms and medication use.
Fasting glucose was slightly above goal on one interval sample and improved on repeat testing. No urgent follow-up action was required beyond routine surveillance.
Serum magnesium was within expected range. Trend remains stable compared with the previous sample.
Complete blood count reviewed with stable hemoglobin, white blood cell count, and platelet count within expected reference ranges. Result supports continuation of the current monitoring plan.

Comprehensive metabolic profile showed electrolytes, renal markers, and liver enzymes without clinically significant abnormalities. Clinical correlation was documented with recent symptoms and medication use.
Lipid panel demonstrated mildly elevated LDL with triglycerides and HDL otherwise acceptable for ongoing lifestyle counseling. No urgent follow-up action was required beyond routine surveillance.
HbA1c remained in the prediabetes or diabetes monitoring range with a small interval improvement compared with prior testing. Trend remains stable compared with the previous sample.
